criterion: error and rollback paths / re-run after a crash
finding: remove_v1_block writes the stripped instruction file before the `after` marker, so a failure between the two writes loses the v1 block on switch-back.
why: If `write_atomic(saved / "after", ...)` never runs (IO error, AV lock, crash), a re-run sees `absent` and never writes `after`; `restore_v1_block` then takes the `kept-backup-dropped` branch and `shutil.rmtree`s the only copy of the removed block, which stays in `original`/`blocks`.
fix: Write `saved/after` (and `blocks`) before replacing the target. A crash then leaves current != after with blocks present, which `restore_v1_block` already handles as `block-present`.
evidence:
write_atomic(target, after)
        write_atomic(saved / "after", after)  /  restore: `if not (saved / "after").exists(): action = "kept-backup-dropped"` ... `shutil.rmtree(saved)` (setup.py:170-171,182)

criterion: error and rollback paths / ordering of restore steps
finding: switch-back dies on the first git-hook backup whose repository or hooks dir no longer exists, so no later restore runs.
why: `shutil.move(keep, target)` raises FileNotFoundError when the saved hooks dir is gone (deleted clone, retired worktree); `main` maps it to exit 2. `restore_v1_git_hooks` runs before settings, Codex config, lavish and the v1-only step, and the backup stays, so every re-run fails the same way.
fix: Skip with action `repo-missing` (keep or drop the backup) when `hooks.parent` is absent. Catch OSError per entry so the other restore steps still run.
evidence: hooks = Path((saved / "place.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) ... if not target.exists(): shutil.move(str(keep), str(target)) (setup.py:297,302-303); `switch_back` calls it at line 416 with no guard

criterion: error and rollback paths / missing files
finding: _common_dir ignores a failed git call, so `Path('')` becomes the cwd and switch-back and the plugin switch write `info/exclude` in the current directory.
why: For a deleted repo, `git -C` fails with empty stdout; `Path('')/'info'/'exclude'` is the relative `info/exclude`. `restore(saved/'exclude', ...)` (line 426) and `_ensure_local_ignored` (line 332) then write into cwd. `_leave_v1_only` also recreates the deleted repo's `.claude/` through `write_claude_local`.
fix: Make `_common_dir` return None on a nonzero git exit. In switch-back, skip a repo whose directory or git dir is gone and report `repo-missing`.
evidence: got = _git(run, repo, "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir"); return Path(got.out.strip()) (setup.py:261-262); used at setup.py:332, 422, 426

finding: switch-back restores Codex config.toml, settings.local.json and info/exclude by whole-file overwrite, discarding everything written since takeover.
why: Codex and Claude Code keep writing these files (project trust entries, permission grants). The instruction-file restore handles divergence (`appended`), but `restore()` writes the takeover-time copy over them or deletes the file when the backup is `.absent`.
fix: Restore only the keys setup changed (the plugin `enabled` values, the exclude line). Or compare the current file with the post-switch content and report `conflict` instead of overwriting, as the git-hook restore does.
evidence: if saved.exists(): write_atomic(target, saved.read_bytes()) / if absent.exists(): if target.exists(): target.unlink() (places.py:103-110); called at setup.py:424-428. Ledger D-9 chose byte-identical restore.

criterion: error and rollback paths / partial-failure handling
finding: Inputs for the plugin step are first read after the v1 block is removed and the git hooks are moved, and a decode or parse error escapes as exit 2 with no step report.
why: A non-UTF-8 Codex config.toml makes `decode('utf-8')` raise. `takeover` has no try around its steps and `main` prints only `unreadable-input`, so the developer sees no sign that the block, hooks and Claude settings already changed.
fix: Read and validate every plugin input (Claude layers, Codex config) before the first destructive step. Alternatively catch per step in `takeover` and return the completed steps with ok false.
evidence: text = config.read_bytes().decode("utf-8") (setup.py:366); steps loop (491-495) and `except (ValueError, OSError)` (566-568)

finding: write_atomic gives the replaced file default permissions and replaces a symlinked target with a regular file.
why: The tmp file takes the default umask mode. `~/.claude.json` and the Codex config can hold the Jira token, and `store_jira_values` writes a backup copy of `~/.claude.json` the same way, so on POSIX a 0600 file becomes a 0644 file and a new 0644 copy appears (inferred: the source mode is not read here). A dotfile-managed symlink to CLAUDE.md or config.toml is replaced by a plain file.
fix: Copy the original mode onto the tmp file before `os.replace`. Resolve a symlink target first. Create the backup with 0600.
evidence:
tmp.write_bytes(data)
    os.replace(tmp, path) (places.py:79-80); write_atomic(saved, path.read_bytes()) (jira_values.py:86)

finding: The ~/.claude.json backup is rewritten on every `secrets` run, so a second run overwrites the original with the already-edited file.
why: The docstring says back up a file before its edit, and every other backup uses `backup_once`. ADR-0008 says every write keeps a backup. Here an unconditional `write_atomic` makes the second run's backup the first run's output.
fix: Use `backup_once(path, saved)`.
evidence:
saved = places.backup / "claude-user-config" / "claude.json"
        write_atomic(saved, path.read_bytes()) (jira_values.py:85-86)

finding: A failed `npm ls` reads as 'lavish not installed' and is recorded permanently as prior `none`; switch-back then uninstalls the developer's own lavish-axi.
why: `lavish_version` returns None for npm missing (127), a timeout (126), unparsable output or a real absence. `install_lavish_pin` writes the record once, and `has_backup` blocks any later correction.
fix: Tell 'package absent' from 'npm failed': record only when `npm ls` ran (exit 0 or 1 with JSON). Otherwise return a lavish-failed result and write no record.
evidence: prior = lavish_version(run, env) ... if not has_backup(record): record.write_text((prior or "none") + "\n") (tools.py:190-194); restore: `if prior == "none": ... npm uninstall -g` (tools.py:211-213)

finding: `_scalar` keeps a trailing YAML comment in the value, so the copy silently drops the section that kind key names.
why: `tracker: github-issues  # which` yields the value `github-issues  # which`. That is not a key in `blocks`, so the `github-issues:` section is not copied and `copy_v1_config` still returns ok. Separately, `_blocks` ends a block at an unindented `- item` line (line 41), so a valid unindented sequence is cut short.
fix: Strip ` #...` comments in `_scalar`. Treat a column-0 `- ` line as a continuation of the open block.
evidence: value = block.split(b"\n", 1)[0].split(b":", 1)[1].strip().decode("utf-8"); return value.strip("'\"") (repo_config.py:51-52)

criterion: blast radius: write outside the contract's named targets
finding: Plugin switch appends a line to the repository's shared git `info/exclude`, a write the contract never names. It also stays after switch-back.
why: `_common_dir` resolves the git common dir, so in a linked-worktree layout the line reaches every worktree of the repository. Switch-back keeps the line on purpose (D-10), so the change the contract says switch-back restores is not undone. The plan ledger records only the keep-at-switch-back choice (D-10). It has no decision for adding the line, and SKILL.md never mentions the exclude edit or the settings.local.json file it covers.
fix: Add a plan-ledger decision for the exclude write itself (not only D-10's keep choice) and name it in SKILL.md. Or drop `_ensure_local_ignored` and report 'settings.local.json is not ignored' to the developer.
evidence: setup.py:337 `write_atomic(exclude, old + sep + b"/.claude/settings.local.json\n")`. The contract's ADR-0008 excerpt lists the writes (v1 block, git hook stubs, project personal settings, global Codex, lavish, rg) and none is git `info/exclude`. The integration row says "switch-back → every file byte-identical to before"; test_integration.py:102 instead asserts `exclude.read_bytes() == files[exclude] + b"/.claude/settings.local.json\n"`.

finding: The no-write idempotency check compares file mtime, so a rewrite in the same clock tick still passes.
why: The two calls run back to back, and on a coarse-mtime filesystem a rewrite that changes nothing leaves the mtime equal, so the test can pass while the code writes. Inferred, not run.
fix: Set the file mtime to an old value with os.utime before the second call, or spy on write_atomic, then assert it was not called. test_proof.py:70 already uses the os.utime approach.
evidence: stamp = local.stat().st_mtime_ns ... assert again["ok"] and not again["written"] and local.stat().st_mtime_ns == stamp

finding: The Codex refusal to leave both plugins enabled has no test.
why: The acceptance bullet requires setup to refuse leaving both afk and afkv2 enabled on Codex, but only the Claude refusal (test_plugin_switch.py:47) is exercised. The Codex error branch at setup.py:381 never runs.
fix: Add a test where the config edit is stubbed out (as in the Claude test) or the fake list returns both enabled, then assert ok False and code both-enabled.
evidence: Acceptance: "setup refuses to leave both `afk` and `afkv2` enabled"; Codex tests assert only ok True (test_plugin_switch.py:57, 71, 78).

finding: takeover and switch_back are tested only on the all-green path and the proof-refused path.
why: Nothing tests a step failing mid-takeover (bad-block, plugin both-enabled, lavish-install-failed) stopping the later steps, and nothing tests a re-run continuing where it stopped. SKILL.md promises "a re-run continues where it stopped". The switch-back not-ok branches (hook conflict, lavish-restore-failed, install record kept) are also untested.
fix: Add takeover cases using FakeRunner.npm_fails and a broken block, asserting ok False, which steps ran, and a clean second run. Add a switch-back case with a hook conflict that asserts ok False and the install record kept.
evidence: setup.py:491-498 stops at the first failed step; setup.py:413-429 sets ok False on conflict; grep of tests/setup finds no test that reaches either.

finding: Removal and restore are tested only with a single block per file.
why: v1 writes up to four blocks per file (v1_facts.BLOCK_NAMES). The multi-block cursor loop in remove_v1_block and the join in the "appended" restore path have no test. The restore branches "block-present" and "kept-backup-dropped" are also untested.
fix: Add a file with behaviors and investigation blocks and text between them. Assert exact bytes after removal, after restore, and after restore following an edit.
evidence: test_rule_block.py:33-69 use only v1_block(); the two-block input exists only in the find_blocks test at line 19-23. setup.py:131-170 loops over blocks.

finding: The "byte for byte" config copy is tested only with LF line ends; CRLF is never tested.
why: _blocks rewrites the last line of each block to LF, so a CRLF v1 config is copied with mixed line ends. This breaks the module's byte-for-byte claim. The rule-block tests already treat CRLF as a real case on Windows.
fix: Add a CRLF V1 config case, assert the copied blocks are byte-identical, and fix repo_config if the test fails.
evidence: repo_config.py:3-4 "moved as its whole top-level block, byte for byte"; repo_config.py:47 `v.rstrip(b"\r\n") + b"\n"`; V1 fixture test_repo_config.py:3-6 has LF only.

finding: The registry PATH and user-environment writers have no test, though they hold dedupe and registry-kind logic.
why: windows_user_path_adder (dedupe by normcase and expandvars, preserves REG_EXPAND_SZ) and windows_user_env_setter edit the user's registry. Their branches are unreachable in tests because they import winreg directly.
fix: Import winreg through an injectable name, or put a fake winreg module in sys.modules in-process. Test already-present, absent-key and REG_EXPAND_SZ-preserved cases.
evidence: tools.py:123-142 and jira_values.py:100-105; grep of tests/setup finds no reference to winreg, windows_user_path_adder or windows_user_env_setter.

finding: The ask-and-store test asserts only that JIRA_BASE_URL was stored.
why: The token and email are the point of the test, but a regression that drops either one passes. The name says "asks once" but nothing counts the prompts.
fix: Assert stored == {all three keys} (the token compared in-test, not printed), and count the ask calls.
evidence: assert answer["ok"] and stored["JIRA_BASE_URL"] == "https://s.atlassian.net"

finding: The gitignore line is added only when this run wrote the settings file, so a re-run after a crash between the two steps never adds it.
why: The re-run sees `written` False and skips `_ensure_local_ignored`. The local settings file then shows in `git status` and can be committed.
fix: Call `_ensure_local_ignored` whenever the local file exists, independent of `written`.
evidence: ignored_now = written and _ensure_local_ignored(repo, run, saved if with_backup else None)

criterion: Hook proof: without proof setup reports why (PRD AC-015)
finding: The SKILL tells the agent to relay each line of proof.reasons, but the no-install-record refusal has no reasons key.
why: prove_hook returns _error("no-install-record", ..., proved=False) with no reasons list, so the report step has nothing to read. The reason sits in the top-level error.
fix: Return reasons=[reason] in the no-install-record answer, or have the SKILL name error.reason as the fallback.
evidence: setup.py:228 return _error("no-install-record", "run `setup.py prepare` first", proved=False); SKILL.md:48 "each line of `proof.reasons`"

finding: Setup writes ownership to .afkv2/config.yaml in an ownership: own/shared grammar that no reader in this branch confirms (unverified).
why: The S1 config reader (afkv2/scripts/afkv2_config.py) is absent from this tree. Its contract names no file or ownership grammar. The AC-020 ownership behavior therefore rests on an unchecked agreement that D-6 defers to S4 0016.
fix: Keep D-6 open until S4 0016 runs setup output through the real reader, and record that cross-check as an explicit IOU in the plan.
evidence: AFKV2_CONFIG = (".afkv2", "config.yaml"); plan-s1/0001-skeleton-manifests-hooks.md:42 "resolves spec folder, tracker kind and ownership from `.afkv2`" (no file name or grammar)

finding: The fake `codex plugin list` builds its table from production codex_config_state, so the Codex list seam test can echo a shared parse error.
why: The table layout is invented here and in test_parse_codex_list_reads_columns (test_plugin_switch.py:86). Only the owner-run live-check doc covers real CLI output.
fix: Have the fake return a literal table captured from the real CLI, and keep the live check as the guard for that layout.
evidence: state = plugins.codex_config_state(self.places.codex_config.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) ... rows.append(f"{plugin_id:<20}{status:<21}1.0.0    local")

finding: prepare failure paths have no test: winget_installs and the rg failure branches are never used.
why: winget_installs is never set False. rg-install-failed, rg-not-on-every-shell, a Python 2 rejection, and prepare exiting 1 are untested. SKILL.md step 2 depends on the red rg.shells report.
fix: Add tests setting winget_installs False and a shell that stays red after the path add. Assert the error code and that the CLI exits 1.
evidence: tools.py:105-109 and tools.py:117-119 are unreached; the only winget_installs hit in tests is conftest.py:44,64.

finding: The e2e test is one long multi-behavior test, its comment misstates the scenario, and it loops with a `continue`.
why: The comment says "The hook fired before setup's install record", but no fired record exists, so only the never-fired branch runs and the stale-record branch is covered only by the unit test. Roulette-style asserts and the `if ... continue` loop at lines 96-99 make a failure hard to place.
fix: Fix the comment or add a real stale-record step. Split the idempotency and switch-back phases into separate tests, and assert the expected set of files explicitly instead of skipping with `continue`.
evidence: # The hook fired before setup's install record: no proof ...  (no fire() call before line 57); `if path in (places.codex_config, exclude): continue`

finding: The ownership, secrets, copy-config failure and not-a-repo CLI paths are untested through main.
why: The argparse nargs="*" handling of --own and --shared, --skip, --repo and the not-a-repo exit 2 have no test. Only the module functions are tested.
fix: Add CLI cases for `ownership --own a --shared b`, `ownership --skip` and a non-repo directory.
evidence: setup.py:559-561 and 544-546; tests call main only for prepare, copy-config, takeover, status and switch-back.

finding: The hook proof's two inputs are defined only by the fixtures: the `hook-fired-<provider>.txt` path and the prebuilt core-behaviors file layout.
why: No producer exists in the afkv2 tree to check against, so a mismatch with the real hook would make takeover always refuse. That is a safe failure, but nothing in the suite would catch it.
fix: When the hook slice lands, add a test that builds or reads the real shipped file and fired-record path and feeds them to prove_hook.
evidence: grep of afkv2 outside tests/setup finds `afkv2-core-behaviors` only in setup.py and SKILL.md. Layout rule is from ADR 0005: "The text starts and ends with `afkv2-core-behaviors begin|end <sha12>`". Unverified: the hook's actual file name and location.
